transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is… my talking, mostly. It gets all tangled up when I’m trying to explain something. Like I’ll start telling somebody about the keys, because the keys are important, you know, and then it turns into me talking about jail, and then somehow I’m on the prayer rug, and then I’m trying to explain it with chess pieces, like the pieces show where things are supposed to go. And people look at me like I lost them.

I don’t mean to jump around. In my head it feels connected, like one thing leads to the next, but when it comes out of my mouth, folks say they can’t follow what I’m saying. They tell me, “Slow down,” or “What are you talking about?” and then I get frustrated because I’m trying to explain it right. So, yeah… that’s why I’m here. My words don’t come out in the order people need them to.
Have you had a time when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… yes, that happens. Not just like, “Oh, I stayed up too late watching TV,” not that kind of tired-stupid thing. I mean I can sleep maybe two hours, three hours, and then I’m up before the sun is even really there, and I feel… fresh. Like my body got charged up somehow.

I’ll get up and start thinking about everything I need to do, like the floors, the trash, the hallways, what order things should be done in, who’s leaving what where. I’ll start planning work in my head like sleep is for other people, like they need it but I don’t really need it right then. And it doesn’t feel bad at first. It feels like, okay, I’m ahead of everybody, I can get moving, I can get things lined up before the day even starts.

People tell me that’s not normal, because they say if they only slept two or three hours they’d be dragging, but I don’t always feel that way. Sometimes I feel ready, like I already had a full night even though I know I didn’t.
Have there been times when you were hearing or believing unusual things even when your mood was not especially high or energized?

Yeah… that’s happened. That’s the part that makes it harder to explain, because it wasn’t always when I was all up and moving fast or not sleeping. There were weeks where I was more calm, like I wasn’t feeling especially high, and I wasn’t down in a deep hole either. I was just… regular enough, I guess, doing my days.

But even then, for more than a couple weeks, I was still hearing this man in the vents. Not like just a pipe knocking once and I got startled. I mean I’d be in the building and I’d hear him up there, like he was talking or making himself known through the vents. And I kept thinking people in the building were signaling about me too, like little things they did or the way things were placed meant something about me. It felt organized, like they knew and were passing messages around.

And that was when my mood wasn’t especially anything big. That’s why I can’t just say it only happens when I’m charged up, because it doesn’t. It can keep going even when I’m calmer.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… yes. I mean, I don’t always know how to count the days right, because when I’m in it the days kind of stack on top of each other, but it’s been more than just one bad morning, you know? There are stretches where most of the day feels like I’m carrying something heavy inside me.

On my bad days, after morning prayer, I’ll just sit there on the edge of the bed. I’ll be awake, I’ll know I’m supposed to get up and wash up and put myself together, but I feel heavy and empty at the same time. Like my body is sitting there, but the reason to move is gone. I’ll look at my clothes or think about going outside, and it feels like, what’s the point? Not in a dramatic way, just… flat. Like there’s no use cleaning myself up or stepping out the door.

And it can stay with me most of the day. It’s not like I’m sad for five minutes and then I’m fine. It hangs around. I can sit too long, think too much, and everything feels far away, like the day is happening but I’m not really in it.
Looking across the whole time you’ve been having these problems, have you spent most of that time feeling depressed?

Most of the whole time? I don’t think most, no… not if I’m counting it right. It feels like a lot when I’m inside it, because those heavy stretches take over everything, but when I look across the whole illness, I’d say the depressed periods added up to maybe around seven months.

Not all at once necessarily in my head, but altogether, those times where I was really weighed down and hopeless, like the day had no use to it… that’s maybe about seven months total. So it’s been a big part, and it feels severe when it’s happening, but I wouldn’t say it’s been the majority of the whole time.
